title: Lifting generators regular in the target along a generator-space isomorphism
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be nonzero commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $c:R\to S$ be a local ring homomorphism, meaning $c(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, inducing an isomorphism $k=R/\mathfrak m\xrightarrow{\sim}S/\mathfrak n$. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a finitely generated ideal, put $J=IS$, and suppose that the induced map $\beta:I/\mathfrak mI\to J/\mathfrak nJ$, $a\bmod\mathfrak mI\mapsto c(a)\bmod\mathfrak nJ$, is a $k$-linear isomorphism. Suppose $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathfrak n$ is an $S$-regular sequence generating $J$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then $y_1,\ldots,y_r$ modulo $\mathfrak nJ$ form a $k$-basis of $J/\mathfrak nJ$. For every $k$-basis $\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_r$ of $I/\mathfrak mI$ and every choice of lifts $f_j\in I$, the $f_j$ generate $I$, and $c(f_1),\ldots,c(f_r)$ is an $S$-regular sequence generating $J$. Such bases and lifts exist, including the empty basis when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (1), together with Algebra Tags 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), 061S (lemma-quasi-regular-regular), and 00DV (lemma-NAK); agent-formulated lifting consequence of a specified isomorphism on generator spaces.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-ideal-residue-basis-prescribed-generator] with ring $S$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and sequence $y$. Its first assertion gives the residue basis $([y_i])$ of $J/\mathfrak nJ$ over $S/\mathfrak n$, hence over $k$ through the specified residue-field isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), degree one, and 00SE (lemma-ci-well-defined), final paragraph.

proof.text: The inverse images $\beta^{-1}([y_i])$ are a basis of $I/\mathfrak mI$: a linear relation maps to a relation in the basis $([y_i])$, and any vector maps to its linear combination. Choose representatives in $I$ using the quotient map. This proves existence of a basis with $r$ entries and of lifts. Now fix ANY such basis $([f_i])$ and ANY representatives $f_i\in I$.

source.place: Elementary basis transport through the stipulated linear isomorphism and quotient representatives.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with $A=R$ and finite module $M=I$. Since the residues of the $f_i$ span $I/\mathfrak mI$, the lifts generate $I$. Put $x_i=c(f_i)$. If $a=\sum a_if_i\in I$, then $c(a)=\sum c(a_i)x_i$, so extending ideals gives $J=IS=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Also $x_i\in\mathfrak n$ since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $c$ is local.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (8), followed by the definition of ideal extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-local-generating-tuples] over the nonzero local ring $S$ to the finite $S$-module $J$ and the two generating tuples $y$ and $x$, both of length $r$. It supplies an invertible matrix $P\in\mathrm{GL}_r(S)$ with $x=Py$. Finiteness of $J$ follows from either displayed generating tuple. Write $B=S/J$; reducing $P$ and its inverse modulo $J$ gives mutually inverse matrices $\bar P$ and $\overline{P^{-1}}$ over $B$.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), local generating-tuple consequence; compare More on Algebra Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (1).

proof.text: By [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], the map $\theta_y:B[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\operatorname{gr}_J(S)$ sending $T_i$ to $[y_i]_1$ is an isomorphism. Define $\alpha(T_i)=\sum_j\bar P_{ij}T_j$ and let $\alpha$ fix $B$. Substitution using $\overline{P^{-1}}$ is its inverse: on each variable either composite is the corresponding identity-matrix row. On coefficients and variables $\theta_y\alpha$ agrees with $\theta_x$, since $[x_i]_1=\sum_j\bar P_{ij}[y_j]_1$. Thus the canonical graded map $\theta_x$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), part (1); explicit invertible linear substitution as in More on Algebra Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-quasi-regular-noetherian-local] to $A=S$, $b=r$, and the tuple $x$. The ring $S$ is nonzero Noetherian local, every $x_i\in\mathfrak n$ by Step 3, and its canonical polynomial-to-graded map is an isomorphism by Step 5. Hence $x$ is $S$-regular; Step 3 already proves it generates $J$. For $r=0$, the original empty tuple gives $J=0$, so $\beta$ gives $I/\mathfrak mI=0$ and Step 3 gives $I=0$. All matrices and polynomial substitutions then have zero variables, and the empty sequence is regular because $S\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 061S (lemma-quasi-regular-regular), with M=S; empty case by the definition of regular sequence.

lean.statement: theorem lift_regular_generators_through_fibre {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] (c : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom c] (σ : (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ≃+* (S ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S)) (hσ : ∀ a : R, σ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) (c a)) (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hIfg : I.FG) (β : (I ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R I))) →ₛₗ[σ.toRingHom] ((I.map c) ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S • (⊤ : Submodule S (I.map c))))) (hβbij : Function.Bijective β) (hβ : ∀ a : I, β (Submodule.Quotient.mk a) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨c a, Ideal.mem_map_of_mem c a.property⟩ : I.map c)) (r : ℕ) (y : Fin r → I.map c) (hy : ∀ i : Fin r, (y i).val ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) (hyreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular S (List.ofFn (fun i ↦ (y i).val))) (hygen : Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ (y i).val)) = I.map c) : (∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (I ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R I))), ∀ i : Fin r, β (b i) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (y i)) ∧ (∀ (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (I ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R I)))) (f : Fin r → I), (∀ i : Fin r, Submodule.Quotient.mk (f i) = b i) → Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ (f i).val)) = I ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular S (List.ofFn (fun i ↦ c (f i))) ∧ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ c (f i))) = I.map c) ∧ (∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (I ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R I)))) (f : Fin r → I), ∀ i : Fin r, Submodule.Quotient.mk (f i) = b i)
